terms.comment: Its first sense is a mine or quarry, and the convict’s work in one (damnātus in metallum, Plin. Ep. 2.11.8); the metal dug from it is a sense of Vergil and Pliny (Lewis & Short). Latin often names the metal instead: aes for copper and bronze, ferrum for iron and steel (see steel).
Pliny’s adjective; as a noun, a miner. Something made of metal is usually named by the metal: ferreus, aēneus, aureus.

phrases.latin: fērācem frūgum, oleī, vīnī, equōrum metallōrumque omnium generum
phrases.english: rich in grain, oil, wine, horses and metals of every kind (of Spain)

phrases.latin: Illud aēneum cum pistillō ejusdem metallī.
phrases.english: That bronze one, with the pestle of the same metal.
